newsitem.title: USA: Novelist Bellow launches third literary journal.
newsitem.headline: Novelist Bellow launches third literary journal.

text.p: Nobel Prize-winning author Saul Bellow and his literary collaborator of 45 years, Boston University professor Keith Botsford, have just launched their third magazine, "The Republic of Letters."
Bellow, 81, said at a launch party in Boston that the magazine, now in bookstores, will come out "as often as we have good enough material to fill it."
"We'll try to come out quarterly if we can, but if we can't, then we can't," he said late on Thursday.

The first issue, which Botsford said was "thrown together," is 40 pages and features an excerpt from Bellow's work-in-progress, "View from Intensive Care" as well as works by Emilio Lascano Tegui, John Auerback and Sean Jackson.
Bellow, who is also teaching this spring at Boston University, and Botsford, 70, collaborated to launch the literary magazines "The Noble Savage" in the 1960s and "Anon" in the 1970s.
Both magazines have ceased publication, but they did help establish such writers as Robert Coover and Thomas Pynchon.

Asked why the two have a pattern of establishing literary journals every few years, Bellow said; "In my case it is a defence against death. If I do a thing every 15 years it makes me think I'll live to do it again."
